clue.text: Country that informally gives boozer heart

parts.note: the middle two letters of 'boozer' are O and Z, and Oz is the casual name for this country

explanation.surface: A nation whose slang name sits at the centre of a word for a hard drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: No letters are built: the clue asks for the country whose informal name, Oz, is the heart (middle letters) of 'boozer'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nation, the one Australians and others call Oz in casual speech.

clue.text: Result of one who was fired up for a sporting contest?

definitions.text: Result of one who was fired up
definitions.meaning: what remains after a cremation, when a body has been burnt
the cricket Test series played between England and Australia

explanation.surface: What an over-excited player leaves behind in a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired up' looks like 'excited' but means literally burnt. The Ashes is the long-running cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation leaves remains of burnt powder, and the same word names a famous cricket trophy series.

clue.text: Rows over press-ganging school's head for assembly

indicators.note: press-ganging forces someone in, so one letter is drafted into the reversed word
over signals that the word for rows is turned round, read the other way

parts.note: rows in the sense of loud quarrels or din, i.e. noises

indicators.note: the head of the word school's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Arguments about forcing a headteacher into a school assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns NOISES into SESION, and 'press-ganging' drafts S (the head of 'school's') into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a meeting or sitting of a body, as in a parliamentary or court sitting.

clue.text: Broadcast put back

definitions.meaning: to transmit a programme, as a station passes a signal on
laid again, as a carpet is re-laid after being lifted

explanation.surface: A programme transmitted and then replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is RE-LAY: to lay something down again.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay transmits a signal onward, and re-laying is placing something down a second time.

clue.text: Year One, being involved in Latin: state "poetic"

indicators.note: being involved in says the year-and-one letters sit inside what follows

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A first-year Latin student declares a passage poetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved in' places year-and-one between the Latin letter and the state, so the container is split by the colon in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is expressive and song-like, the quality of verse.

clue.text: Orchestrated UN's clash with second German political union

indicators.note: orchestrated means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A United Nations confrontation was engineered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestrated' rearranges UNSCLASH into ANSCHLUS, then S for second follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1938 annexation of Austria by Nazi Germany is known by this German term for joining.

clue.text: Advantage of top-cut grass

indicators.note: top-cut means the head of the plant word is chopped off

parts.note: sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground

explanation.surface: The benefit of having the lawn trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-cut' removes S from SEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means holding a slight advantage.

clue.text: Sense a change, taking millions all together

indicators.note: taking means the shuffled letters take in another letter
change tells us the letters of these words are altered into a new order

parts.note: M stands for million(s)

explanation.surface: Feeling a shift as millions of people act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SENSEA into ENASSE, and 'taking' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means as a body or group, everyone at once.

clue.text: Digging group entertaining fancy diner?

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the group word holds the other letters

parts.note: a gang is a group of people

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A digging crew hosting a smart restaurant customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the anagram signal on 'diner', and 'entertaining' makes the group hold the result; the question mark flags that 'Digging' is a hobby, not excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: Working the soil of a plot with spade and fork is an example of this hobby.

clue.text: Canadian resort artist

definitions.meaning: a ski resort in British Columbia, Canada

explanation.surface: A painter associated with a Canadian ski destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a ski town north of Vancouver and to the painter of 'Whistler's Mother'.

clue.text: Grey hat tipped or removed

indicators.note: removed says those reversed letters are taken out of the hat word

parts.note: a sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat

indicators.note: tipped means turned over, so the little word or is read backwards

explanation.surface: A grey hat raised in greeting or taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' turns OR into RO, and 'removed' takes RO off SOMBRERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey, as in a dull or gloomy mood or colour, is close in sense to dark and solemn.

clue.text: Cross, if Yorkshire holds become fixed

indicators.note: holds signals that the run of words contains the answer within it

explanation.surface: An angry Yorkshire stands firm and refuses to change.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'crOSS IF Yorkshire'.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to bone, and figuratively to grow rigid and inflexible in one's habits.

clue.text: Wasn't the only entertainer to fashion hoods etc

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so these letters are made into a new form

explanation.surface: A designer shared the credit for making hoods and such.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges HOODSETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing the role of presenting a show with another person means one was not the sole entertainer.

clue.text: Key sporting event about to return

parts.note: an Open is a tournament open to all, as in golf or tennis

indicators.note: to return means the about word comes back the other way

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A major sporting event about to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, like a tin- or bottle-opener, is a device that unlocks or opens.

clue.text: Pointedly edit written work?

parts.note: editing a text by adding full stops, commas and other points

explanation.definitionFit: Inserting points such as stops and commas into text is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Figures on ancestral houses echoing quality

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the run of words holds the answer

explanation.surface: Statues standing in grand old family homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'figuRES ON ANCEstral'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is the quality of a sound that is deep, full and reverberating.

clue.text: Hacked email about eastern country's US-style disease

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the others
hacked means cut up roughly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, a country

explanation.surface: A hacked email concerning an eastern nation's illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacked' rearranges EMAIL into LEMIA, which goes 'about' E and UK. 'US-style' points to the American spelling, without the extra A of British leukaemia.
explanation.definitionFit: This blood cancer is a disease, spelt here the American way.

clue.text: Breakdown is its own possible cure

parts.note: the talking therapy used to treat a nervous collapse has the same name as a breaking-down into parts

explanation.surface: A mental collapse that might heal itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakdown' reads as a nervous collapse, which a Freudian talking cure might treat; that cure's name also means separating something into its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking something down into components to examine them is a close synonym.

clue.text: Character who drowned, one grabbed by shark possibly

indicators.note: grabbed by means the one letter is held inside the shark word

parts.note: a loan shark is one kind of lender, hence possibly
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A drowning victim seized by a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see Hero and drowned in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The youth of the Hero legend is a mythical figure who died in the water.

clue.text: Senior, quaintly rotten inside, whose clients put something on the horses

definitions.text: whose clients put something on the horses

indicators.note: inside says the rotten word goes within the senior letters

parts.note: addle is an old-fashioned adjective for rotten, as in an addled egg

explanation.surface: An old person, decaying within, whose customers bet on races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put something on the horses' looks like betting, but means fitting saddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes saddles serves riders who fit his goods onto their mounts.

clue.text: Runners on this start to slow step

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a ledge is a step-like shelf

explanation.surface: Athletes slowing down at the start of a stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' are not athletes but the blades a sledge glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled rides on two runners, so it is the thing those runners are on.

clue.text: Vengeful character taking pick to Egyptian god

parts.note: to elect is to pick or choose
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A vengeful figure selecting an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra in Greek myth sought revenge for the murder of her father Agamemnon.

clue.text: Eat it and dancing is hit

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eat it and dance: that is a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges EATITAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit a target or goal is to reach or achieve it.

clue.text: Fold back electronic snail mail reply facilitator (Roman Catholic)

indicators.note: back says the whole string of letters is read the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, sent so that the recipient can reply by post

explanation.surface: A folded e-mail, envelope and Catholic note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ESAERC round to give the answer. An SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, enclosed in Britain so someone can reply by post.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding, so the fold itself.

clue.text: Round hook?

definitions.meaning: a song for several voices where each enters in turn, like a canon, especially a humorous one
to hook a fish is to land it

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a comic song sung in canon and the act of seizing or hooking something.

clue.text: Dies in distress — Kay intervenes — sent heavenward

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the letter is placed among the others
in distress means in a battered state, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Kay is the spelt-out name of the letter K

explanation.surface: Someone dies in agony while Kay steps in, sent up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' turns DIES into SIED, and K 'intervenes'. 'Sent heavenward' looks like death, but means a ball hit high.
explanation.definitionFit: To sky a ball is to strike it high into the air, upward toward the sky.

clue.text: Miss relief — in pieces

indicators.note: in says the relief word sits inside the pieces word

parts.note: chess pieces are called men
aid is help or relief

explanation.surface: A young woman's relief has fallen apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' are chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an unmarried young woman, addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Act without control and don't spare a tear

definitions.meaning: to go all out with no restraint
a rip is a tear, so letting the rip happen is not sparing it

explanation.surface: Behave wildly, and don't hold back the tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' reads as weeping but is the rip of torn cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go at full speed or unrestrained, and literally to allow a tear to happen.

clue.text: Put up with no bull!

definitions.meaning: on the stock market, a pessimist is the opposite of a bull

explanation.surface: Tolerate it: no nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' looks like nonsense, but a bull is a market optimist, the opposite of a pessimistic trader.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to endure; a bear in finance is a seller expecting prices to fall, not a bull.

clue.text: So astronauts may be bound to get tense, being overwhelmed by hardware malfunction

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by means the tense letter is swallowed by the other letters
a malfunction puts the hardware out of order, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Space crews get anxious when their equipment fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malfunction' rearranges HARDWARE into EARHWARD, and T goes inside, 'overwhelmed by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts returning home are heading toward our planet, bound in that direction.
